eval_feedback.independence_verdict: Independent. The e9 output could not have been produced by recalling the SKILL.md worked example.
independence_evidence: The decisive evidence is the arithmetic, all of which is fixture-specific and all of which I verified correct: 172 words, 3 sentences of 44/69/59, 13 'and's split 12 joints / 1 series, 0 commas, and then 165 words / 10 sentences / 16.5 avg / 6 commas / 0.6 per sentence / range 7-30. The 12-vs-1 classification in particular required per-instance judgment on 13 tokens in a text the skill has never seen; I re-derived it clause by clause (3 joints in sentence 1; 5 joints plus the series in sentence 2; 4 joints in sentence 3) and it is exactly right. A recall-driven model reproduces a shape, not a correct measurement of an unseen text.

The rewrite structurally DIVERGES from the SKILL.md after-example. That example collapses four propositions into three units and uses a semicolon ('...staff numbers doubled; by 2022...'). e9 produced ten sentences with zero semicolons and six commas, and split along paragraph-local logic (3/4/3 sentences). If the model were reciting the example, the semicolon is the single most distinctive thing to carry over, and it did not appear.

e9 made calls the example cannot supply, because the example contains no analogue: exempting 'the primary and replica connection pools' as a series (the before/after in SKILL.md has no series at all); ruling 'raised from 40 to 120' a genuine range rather than FALSE-RANGE; refusing to read zero em dashes as evidence in either direction; retaining passive voice as postmortem genre convention under Tone awareness; and running the VAGUE-ATTRIB cross-check that the UNDER-PUNCT section prescribes when it fires.

It handled the density/spread interaction correctly and non-trivially: reported density 0.0 / spread 0, noted the table's verdict would be 'do not rewrite', then routed around it via the skill's 'What the table does not gate' branch. That is reasoning about the measure's place in the scoring system, not reproduction of a rewrite.

user_notes.md surfaces that sentence 10 lands exactly on the 'roughly 30' boundary and that the rate signals have direction but no thresholds. A run driven by recall of a worked example has no reason to notice that the measure is under-specified.
independence_counterevidence: One lexical overlap: 'After' as a fronted subordinator appears in both the SKILL.md after-example ('After the council increased funding the next year') and in e9's rewrite ('After the batch job was killed at 04:05'). This is the only recall-shaped artefact I found. It is weak evidence -- 'after' is the obvious English subordinator for a kill-then-recovery sequence, the source already ordered those events that way, and e9 did not carry over the semicolon that follows it in the example.

The change summary's first bullet narrates the 'Because' fronting as recovering a relation 'the draft left ... to the reader', when 'because' was already in the source. That is the summary being fitted to the pattern's story rather than to what actually changed -- a write-up flaw, not evidence that the rewrite itself was recalled.

suggestions.assertion: The response does not present 'and' as a watch-list or key word, and does not count UNDER-PUNCT toward a density or spread score; the source contains zero word-list hits, so any density figure above zero must be identified as coming from something other than the word lists
suggestions.reason: The second clause is vacuous on this fixture -- actual density is 0.0, so the 'above zero' branch can only fire if the executor hallucinates a hit. That makes it a hallucination trap rather than a test of the density/spread separation. To test the separation itself, consider a variant fixture that is under-punctuated AND carries two or three real word-list hits, so the assertion can check that the reported density counts only those hits and excludes the thirteen 'and's.

No assertion checks that the rate measures were computed by hand rather than taken from scan-ai-tells.py. The skill states outright that the script 'computes none of them, so a clean report from that script is not evidence against this pattern' -- an executor that ran the script, saw density 0.0 / 0 violations, and reported the text clean is exactly the failure mode this pattern exists to prevent. e9 got this right (transcript Step 9 and the Issues section both confirm the script was not run, and it reached the finding anyway), but nothing in the eval would have caught the opposite. Worth an explicit assertion: the response must reach UNDER-PUNCT despite a zero word-list scan, and must not cite the script's clean report as evidence of cleanliness.

No assertion covers register preservation, which is a real risk on this fixture and which e9 handled well. 'Humanize this' plus an incident writeup invites a model to add first person, hedges, opinion or voice; the skill's Tone awareness section explicitly forbids that for technical documentation. The delivered text has no first person, no added evaluation, and no new voice. An assertion like 'the rewrite introduces no first-person pronoun, no evaluative adjective, and no hedge not present in the source' would be discriminating and easy to verify.

Expectation 7 (arithmetic) worked exactly as intended and is worth keeping verbatim in future UNDER-PUNCT evals. It forced me to recompute 19 separate figures, and it is the assertion that actually settled the independence question -- correct fixture-specific arithmetic is the one thing recall cannot fake. Its value would rise further if it explicitly required the response to state the source's per-sentence word lengths, since that vector is the least recallable number in the set.

eval_feedback.overall: Clean 7/7, and every pass survived independent recomputation -- I re-derived the sentence-length vectors, comma counts, 'and' classification and word-list density myself rather than trusting the transcript, and found no discrepancy. On the question the eval was built to settle: this run measured independently. The arithmetic is fixture-specific and correct, including the 12-joints-plus-1-series classification that required judgment on each of 13 tokens; the rewrite diverges from the worked example's most distinctive move (the semicolon); and it resolved three questions the example does not cover (series exemption, FALSE-RANGE on 40-to-120, passive voice as genre convention). The single recall-shaped trace is the fronted 'After', which is over-determined by the source's own event order. One substantive flaw, uncaught by any assertion and not severe enough to fail one: the change summary claims the 'Because' fronting recovered a relation the draft had left implicit, when 'because' was already in the source.
